evidence: Cic. Sest. 54: bona mea dīripiēbantur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Caecin. 38: bona, fortūnās, possessiōnēs omnium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Almost always the whole of one’s possessions (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 2.87: rēs autem familiāris quaerī dēbet iīs rēbus, ā quibus abest turpitūdō
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 19: multī rem ac fortūnās āmittere

phrases.latin: Rēs autem familiāris quaerī dēbet iīs rēbus, ā quibus abest turpitūdō, cōnservārī autem dīligentiā et parsimōniā, eīsdem etiam rēbus augērī.
phrases.english: Property should be acquired by means that have nothing shameful about them, kept by care and thrift, and increased by the same.

sources: Lewis & Short: bonum · Lewis & Short: familiaris · Lewis & Short: fortuna
